items.title: Ted Piltzecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 10, 2019
items.q: I was surprised when I first read that Aaron Copland, who wrote some really incredible melodies

ctx.x: Yeah. I mean you know in this contemporary world there’s all kinds of ways to approach a conversation. I guess I feel like somewhat of a traditionalist in that sense. I like melodies. They still speak to me. I spend a lot of time trying to shape a melody, as a

composer, that is whole and cohesive and you know it reaches. And I think about why. Aaron Copland said, in ’37 or something, he said, “Well we really don’t know why a melody affects us but you know when it does it’s really good.” Since that time we’ve done a lot of research. And I happen to teach melody writing, which I love to do at both the graduate and undergraduate level. So I’ve thought about this a lot. Now we’ve been able to actually figure out psychologically and sociologically why we like certain…
